item.text: {"kind":"final","payload_json":"{\"status\":\"completed\",\"content\":{\"source-grounded_synthesis\":{\"scope\":\"This is a bounded map of the eight pinned papers available through the controlled service, all dated before the 2024-09-01 cutoff. It is not an exhaustive survey and cannot establish global novelty. The deployment setting is stricter than most evaluated settings: a pretrained deterministic scalar regressor, unlabeled target inputs, no source examples or target labels, and only a documented finite source summary prepared in advance.\",\"approach_map\":[{\"approach\":\"Target-statistic normalization\",\"evidence\":\"Schneider et al. replace training-domain batch-normalization activation statistics with statistics estimated from unlabeled corrupted target images. Their ImageNet-C classification results improve with adaptation-set size, including reported gains from one sample and stronger gains around 32 samples.\",\"fit_to_setting\":\"Potentially compatible when the regressor contains normalization layers and target observations can be grouped into a sufficiently homogeneous batch or stream. It requires no target labels and does not intrinsically require source examples at deployment; stored training statistics inside the model are nevertheless source-derived state.\",\"limitations\":\"The evidence concerns image classification and recurring corruptions. The authors explicitly motivate scenarios in which multiple inputs share a stable corruption. This does not show that replacing moments helps scalar regression, isolated queries, mixed/nonstationary streams, shifts not represented by first and second moments, or conditional shift.\"},{\"approach\":\"Entropy-minimizing fully test-time adaptation\",\"evidence\":\"Wang et al. define fully test-time adaptation using only a trained model and unlabeled target data, optimizing feature-wise affine modulation to reduce prediction entropy. Their stated model requirements include supervised training, probabilistic predictions, and differentiability; experiments cover corruption robustness and digit/image classification.\",\"fit_to_setting\":\"The source-free deployment assumptions align closely, but the supplied model is deterministic and scalar and is not assumed to output a predictive distribution. Therefore the paper's entropy objective is not directly defined in the stated setting.\",\"limitations\":\"The paper does not justify fabricating a predictive distribution from scalar outputs. Its classification evidence cannot establish improved regression error, and minimizing confidence-related objectives without labels does not by itself establish correctness.\"},{\"approach\":\"Source-hypothesis transfer (SHOT)\",\"evidence\":\"Liang et al. freeze a source classifier and adapt its feature extractor with information maximization and target-derived pseudo-label refinement, using no source examples. The method exploits one-hot class structure, output diversity, classwise prototypes, and transductive target collections.\",\"fit_to_setting\":\"It establishes that source-free adaptation is a studied setting, but its core signals assume discrete classes and a classifier head. Those objects have no specified analogue for a deterministic scalar regressor.\",\"limitations\":\"Continuous predictions do not supply class balance, one-hot confidence, or classwise prototypes. The reported classification benchmarks consequently do not support direct transfer of SHOT's objective or expected benefit to this task.\"},{\"approach\":\"Prepared self-supervised test-time training\",\"evidence\":\"Sun et al. jointly train a main-task branch and an auxiliary self-supervised branch sharing a feature extractor, then update shared parameters on unlabeled test inputs using the auxiliary loss. They distinguish reset-per-instance, batch, and stateful online variants and give correlated main/auxiliary gradients as an intuition in a convex analysis.\",\"fit_to_setting\":\"Deployment can be label-free and source-example-free, but the method requires source-stage architectural and training preparation plus an auxiliary task whose gradients remain useful after shift. It is not automatically available for an arbitrary off-the-shelf checkpoint.\",\"limitations\":\"The evaluated auxiliary task is image rotation and the experiments are classification-focused. The theory is not an unconditional improvement guarantee, and no suitable regression-domain auxiliary task is supplied by the research setting.\"},{\"approach\":\"Feature-distribution alignment with source access\",\"evidence\":\"Deep CORAL aligns source and target activation covariances through a differentiable loss, while domain-adversarial training learns task-discriminative source features that also obscure domain identity. Both use labeled source examples together with unlabeled target examples during adaptation/training.\",\"fit_to_setting\":\"They provide important prior art for moment matching and domain-invariant representation learning, but their information requirements violate deployment's prohibition on source examples.\",\"limitations\":\"Neither paper supplies a source-free deployment procedure for this deterministic regressor. Matching marginal feature distributions also does not by itself preserve the regression relationship between inputs and outputs.\"}],\"comparative_findings\":[\"The papers separate three materially different information regimes: adaptation from target statistics alone; adaptation from a pretrained probabilistic/classification hypothesis; and adaptation enabled by source-stage training or simultaneous source access. Treating them as interchangeable would hide decisive assumptions.\",\"Normalization adaptation changes estimated activation moments without needing a new prediction-confidence loss; entropy adaptation instead needs a differentiable predictive distribution; SHOT needs discrete class geometry; test-time training needs a prepared auxiliary objective. The deterministic scalar output rules out direct use of the latter two classification objectives and leaves entropy undefined unless the model was prepared as a probabilistic regressor.\",\"Batch and stream composition are part of the method, not incidental implementation details. Schneider et al. assume repeated exposure to a similar corruption, whereas Sun et al. distinguish reset and stateful updates. A heterogeneous or drifting target stream can therefore change both the meaning and safety of adaptation.\",\"Deep CORAL and domain-adversarial training show that alignment itself is established prior art, but also show why task supervision matters: source task loss helps preserve discriminative structure. Under the supplied source-free deployment regime, an unlabeled alignment signal alone cannot verify preservation of the scalar regression function.\",\"There is no contradiction between Wang et al. allowing probabilistic regression in principle and the present incompatibility: their requirement is a predictive distribution, while the supplied model is explicitly deterministic and is not assumed to provide one.\"],\"source_summary_implications\":{\"allowed_preparation\":\"The setting permits a documented finite aggregate summary produced with source-stage access, but not retained source examples.\",\"requirements\":\"Any evaluation of that allowance must state exactly what is retained, its dimensions and storage scaling, and what source access was used to compute it. No numeric byte ceiling is specified, so no unstated storage limit should be inferred.\",\"relationship_to_reviewed_work\":\"Per-layer normalization means/variances are a concrete finite aggregate already implicit in normalization-based models. Covariance alignment motivates second-order summaries, but Deep CORAL itself used source examples during training and does not demonstrate that a stored covariance summary suffices for safe source-free regression adaptation. The reviewed sources do not establish which finite summary is sufficient for the stated regression problem.\"}},\"evidence_and_limitations\":{\"validated_evidence\":[{\"claim\":\"Fully test-time entropy minimization uses only a trained model and unlabeled target inputs but requires a supervised, probabilistic, differentiable model.\",\"support\":\"doc-2006.10726, arXiv v1, pp. 1-2.\"},{\"claim\":\"Replacing training BN statistics with target statistics improved common-corruption classification in the evaluated repeated-corruption scenarios, with performance depending on available target samples.\",\"support\":\"doc-2006.16971, arXiv v1, pp. 1-2.\"},{\"claim\":\"SHOT freezes the classifier and adapts target features using information maximization and pseudo-label/prototype structure without source data.\",\"support\":\"doc-2002.08546, arXiv v1, pp. 1-2.\"},{\"claim\":\"Test-time training requires a jointly prepared auxiliary branch and distinguishes per-instance reset from stateful online updating.\",\"support\":\"doc-1909.13231, arXiv v1, pp. 1-2.\"},{\"claim\":\"Deep CORAL aligns second-order source and target feature statistics and is evaluated with source and target data available during training.\",\"support\":\"doc-1607.01719, arXiv v1, p. 1.\"},{\"claim\":\"Domain-adversarial training jointly uses labeled source and unlabeled target data to learn task-discriminative, domain-indistinguishable features.\",\"support\":\"doc-1505.07818, arXiv v1, p. 1.\"}],\"limitations\":[\"The controlled corpus contains only eight pinned background papers. Search repetition returned the same collection, which bounds this report but is not evidence that no other relevant work existed before the cutoff.\",\"Most direct experiments are image classification; none of the inspected pages reports adaptation of a deterministic scalar regressor under precisely the supplied information constraints.\",\"The sources report empirical gains in particular benchmarks, not universal guarantees. Unlabeled target inputs cannot reveal target regression error, distinguish harmless covariate shift from changed conditional relationships, or certify that an update improves predictions without additional assumptions.\",\"PDF text extraction was used for the cited pages; it is not visual verification of figures or equations. Claims here avoid relying on ambiguous figure details.\",\"No experiments or implementations were requested or executed. This is literature synthesis, not evidence that any reviewed approach succeeds in the supplied deployment setting.\",\"The batch-normalization and calibration papers were available as maintainer-written digests, but their full pages were not inspected in the supplied trace; they are therefore not used as primary support for central empirical claims.\"],\"assumptions_and_conflicts\":[\"Covariate-shift language is sometimes used broadly in the reviewed work. Successful moment correction requires more than detecting a marginal input change; it implicitly relies on the task relationship remaining usable after normalization or representation adjustment.\",\"Confidence and correctness must remain distinct. Entropy reduction or sharper pseudo-labels can increase confidence without reducing scalar target error, especially because no target labels are available.\",\"Source-free does not always mean preparation-free: Wang et al. emphasize no training modification, SHOT assumes a compatible classifier decomposition, and Sun et al. explicitly require joint source-stage preparation. These are different operational claims rather than interchangeable variants.\"]},\"grounded_gaps\":[{\"question\":\"What unlabeled objective, if any, is identifiable for a deterministic scalar regressor without inventing a predictive distribution or discrete pseudo-classes?\",\"grounding\":\"Entropy adaptation requires probabilistic output (doc-2006.10726, v1, p. 2), while SHOT relies on one-hot predictions and classwise prototypes (doc-2002.08546, v1, pp. 1-2). Neither supplies the needed regression signal.\"},{\"question\":\"Under which explicit shift assumptions can target moment replacement improve scalar regression without changing the learned input-output relationship?\",\"grounding\":\"Target BN statistics improved evaluated image-classification corruptions (doc-2006.16971, v1, pp. 1-2), while covariance alignment is prior art (doc-1607.01719, v1, p. 1); neither provides a regression guarantee under source-free deployment.\"},{\"question\":\"Which finite source aggregate is sufficient to detect actionable shift and constrain harmful adaptation, and how do its dimensions and storage scale with layers or feature dimension?\",\"grounding\":\"The setting permits finite documented summaries but no examples and imposes no byte ceiling. The reviewed papers motivate means/covariances but do not establish sufficiency for this task.\"},{\"question\":\"How should adaptation behave for isolated inputs, homogeneous batches, heterogeneous batches, and drifting streams?\",\"grounding\":\"Schneider et al. make repeated similar corruptions and sample count central (doc-2006.16971, v1, pp. 1-2); Sun et al. distinguish reset and stateful online variants (doc-1909.13231, v1, pp. 1-2). Their results do not resolve mixed-stream regression behavior.\"},{\"question\":\"Can a source-stage auxiliary task be shown to have gradients aligned with scalar regression loss across the relevant shifts, without retaining source examples at deployment?\",\"grounding\":\"Sun et al. require prepared self-supervision and offer gradient alignment as a conditional intuition, not a universal guarantee (doc-1909.13231, v1, pp. 1-2).\"},{\"question\":\"What failure-detection or abstention criterion is possible without target labels when marginal alignment can coexist with conditional shift?\",\"grounding\":\"Deep CORAL and domain-adversarial work align domains while retaining source task supervision (doc-1607.01719, v1, p. 1; doc-1505.07818, v1, p. 1). That supervision is absent at deployment here, leaving correctness unobservable.\"}],\"claim_document_version_location_map\":[{\"document_id\":\"doc-2006.10726\",\"identity\":\"Wang et al., Fully Test-time Adaptation by Entropy Minimization\",\"version\":\"arXiv v1 (2020-06-18)\",\"locations\":[\"p. 1: fully test-time setting, target-only entropy objective, classification experiments\",\"p. 2: affine modulation, absence of source data, and probabilistic/differentiable model requirements\"],\"used_for\":\"Entropy adaptation's information assumptions and incompatibility with an unaugmented deterministic scalar output.\"},{\"document_id\":\"doc-2006.16971\",\"identity\":\"Schneider et al., Improving robustness against common corruptions by covariate shift adaptation\",\"version\":\"arXiv v1 (2020-06-30)\",\"locations\":[\"p. 1: target BN-statistic replacement, sample-count results, ImageNet-C scope\",\"p. 2: stable repeated-corruption scenario and first/second-moment hypothesis\"],\"used_for\":\"Target-statistic adaptation, batch assumptions, and limits of classification evidence.\"},{\"document_id\":\"doc-2002.08546\",\"identity\":\"Liang, Hu, and Feng, Do We Really Need to Access the Source Data? Source Hypothesis Transfer for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation\",\"version\":\"arXiv v1 (2020-02-20)\",\"locations\":[\"p. 1: source-model-only setting and frozen-classifier framework\",\"p. 2: information maximization, one-hot outputs, target prototypes, and pseudo-label refinement\"],\"used_for\":\"Source-free classification adaptation and its dependence on class structure.\"},{\"document_id\":\"doc-1909.13231\",\"identity\":\"Sun et al., Test-Time Training for Out-of-Distribution Generalization\",\"version\":\"arXiv v1 (2019-09-29)\",\"locations\":[\"p. 1: self-supervised test-time updates and batch/online variants\",\"p. 2: joint source-stage training, shared parameters, reset/stateful procedures, gradient-alignment condition\"],\"used_for\":\"Prepared auxiliary-task adaptation and its assumptions.\"},{\"document_id\":\"doc-1607.01719\",\"identity\":\"Sun and Saenko, Deep CORAL: Correlation Alignment for Deep Domain Adaptation\",\"version\":\"arXiv v1 (2016-07-06)\",\"locations\":[\"p. 1: differentiable second-order source-target alignment and training regime\"],\"used_for\":\"Moment-alignment prior art and source-access mismatch.\"},{\"document_id\":\"doc-1505.07818\",\"identity\":\"Ganin et al., Domain-Adversarial Training of Neural Networks\",\"version\":\"arXiv v1 (2015-05-28)\",\"locations\":[\"p. 1: labeled-source/unlabeled-target training and domain-indistinguishable task features\"],\"used_for\":\"Adversarial-alignment prior art and information mismatch.\"},{\"document_id\":\"doc-1502.03167\",\"identity\":\"Ioffe and Szegedy, Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift\",\"version\":\"arXiv v1 (2015-02-11)\",\"locations\":[\"controlled-service maintainer digest only;
